current.text: Washington acquired him from the Lakers for Jaden Hardy and second-round picks.
He is the backup big man behind Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis and comes off the bench.
Davis's health is a question, so he could get 30-minute roles at times.
He now plays with Trae Young in Washington.
Do not automatically expect a big drop in his FG%.
He is no longer the player he was in Phoenix.
Washington is trying to compete, so the late-season rest and minutes cuts of past years should not happen.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both value him at 0 USD and rank him 178 and 194, outside the 144 players we draft, so do not pay anything like the 9 USD he cost in our league last season. As a bench big his projected line is about 10 points and 7 rebounds with a strong FG% and no threes, so he only makes sense as a late punt 3PM piece. Leave him on waivers and watch Davis's health and Ayton's minutes in the first weeks, since the expert says he could get 30-minute roles when Davis is out.
